Hey Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we covered:
- Your primary ask: confirm expected monthly cost for the integration and clarify how Redwood measures usage (tokens vs characters vs requests).
- Typical call pattern you described: UI-driven prompts from clinicians + small follow-ups. You estimated ~1M requests/month with fairly repetitive prompts.

Open items / actions for us:
1) Clarify units (tokens vs characters vs requests) and give a worked example for your typical payload.
2) Show how prompt caching could reduce billed tokens for repeated prompts and estimate impact.
3) Share a light pricing calc (attached) and confirm whether your target unit economics of ~$20 per 1M tokens is correct or if your budget is different.

Quick definitions to avoid confusion:
- Token = the billing unit. Redwood bills per input + output tokens consumed by the model.
- Character = raw text length; roughly ~4 characters ≈ 1 token (varies by language/content).
- Request = an API call. Requests count toward rate limits but are NOT the primary billing unit.

Next steps: I attached a simple calc and included Rishi (SE) to help with model selection + caching setup. If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rishi to walk through a concrete example.

Great questions — useful to make this concrete. Below is a short worked example based on your numbers and some notes on caching behavior.

Quick conversions and assumptions:
- Token ≈ 4 characters (English average). So:
  - 600 characters ≈ 150 tokens (input)
  - 200 characters ≈ 50 tokens (output)
  - total ≈ 200 tokens per request

Costs (example unit economics):
- If we assume a target unit price of $20 per 1M tokens (your target), that implies:
  - $0.00002 per token (i.e., $20 / 1,000,000 tokens)
  - 200 tokens/request × 1,000,000 requests = 200,000,000 tokens -> but your ask was 1M requests/month; check whether you meant 1M requests or 1M tokens.

Two common volume interpretations I see in discovery:
A) 1M requests/month × 200 tokens/request = 200M tokens/month -> at $20 per 1M tokens => 200 × $20 = $4,000/month.
B) 1M tokens/month total -> at 200 tokens/request would be ~5,000 requests/month.

So we should confirm whether your "1M" was requests or tokens. From the call it sounded like requests; the numbers below assume requests.

Caching notes (how it affects billed tokens):
- Full response caching (exact match): if Redwood serves a cached response without calling the model, there are no model tokens billed for that call (no input/output tokens charged). This is the highest potential savings for highly repetitive prompts/templates.
- Partial/prefix caching (KV/prompt caching): caching prefixes or KV cache can avoid recomputing the entire context; if a model call is still required, billed tokens may be reduced (because less input is sent or cached values shorten the effective input). Exact behavior depends on how your prompts are constructed (templated vs dynamic patient data).
- Note: some caching strategies require deterministic prompts (exact same text) or well-structured template keys. Rishi can run a quick simulation on your sample logs to estimate likely hit rates.

Worked cost example (assume 1M requests/month):
- Without caching: 1,000,000 requests × 200 tokens/request = 200,000,000 tokens → 200 × $20 = $4,000/month
- With conservative caching (40% of requests served from cache): billed requests = 600,000 → billed tokens = 600,000 × 200 = 120,000,000 tokens → 120 × $20 = $2,400/month
- With aggressive caching (70% cache hit): billed tokens = 300,000 × 200 = 60,000,000 tokens → 60 × $20 = $1,200/month

Other notes:
- Requests are relevant for rate limit sizing (RPS/throughput) and may affect Dedicated capacity sizing, but they are not the same as billing units.
- Characters are useful for rough planning; tokens are the billing unit and the right number to use for cost estimates.

Next steps: 1) Can you confirm whether your "1M" target was requests or tokens? 2) If requests, can you share a small sample of prompt texts (sanitized) so Rishi can estimate realistic cache hit rates? 3) I attached a simple calc — if you confirm the numbers I’ll schedule a 30-min technical call with Rishi to validate and finalize a pricing recommendation.

If you want, I can also produce a table with model-level delta (e.g., base Llama-2-ish vs higher-quality variants) — that will change $/1M tokens but not the token math itself.

Thanks,
Marissa
